meta.title: Marmoria
meta.description: Govern a Roman city: lay out its streets and districts, bring in water and bread, open workshops and shows, and watch the tents turn into insulae.
meta.titre_seo: Marmoria: build a Roman city, free city-building game
meta.description_seo: Build a Roman city: roads, water, farms, workshops, temples and shows. Your people move up from tents to grand insulae. Free management game for ages 13+.
meta.presentation: Marmoria is a city-building game where you govern a Roman city seen from above, in relief. You lay out roads and districts, then settlers arrive along the road from Rome and pitch their tents. Everything travels through the streets: market women, prefects, priests, teachers, doctors and actors make their rounds, and every house they serve grows, from a tent to an imperial palace. Farms, quarries and workshops supply food, pottery, furniture, oil and wine, which caravans and ships trade with the cities of the Empire. You keep an eye on fire, work, taxes and crime, keep five gods happy and answer the emperor; when invaders come, you raise cohorts. The campaign has 17 maps over 10 tiers, from Ostia to Athens or Eburacum; from the fourth tier on, you pick a peaceful or a military province.
meta.regles: Goal: meet the mission's targets: population, then culture, prosperity, peace and the emperor's favour. With a mouse, pick a building in the left menu, then click or drag on the map; right-click for info, scroll wheel to zoom, arrow keys to move around, R to rotate the view, P or Esc to pause. On a touch screen, swipe, then tap Confirm; two fingers pan and zoom, and a long press shows info. Each mission earns up to 3 stars: winning, getting no bailout from the emperor, and winning before the target date. An empty, broke city is lost, and so is a governor the emperor keeps in disgrace for too long. Tap a fort, then "Send" and a spot on the map, to lead its cohort.
meta.competences: city planning, budget management, anticipating risks, reading data
meta.jaquette_alt: Two marble temples, one white and one pink, among gardens, shacks, tents and a fountain in the sun

textes.titre.consigne: Lay out roads and housing, then meet your people's needs: water, food, temples, shows. Every need you meet makes their homes grow and fills your coffers.
textes.outil.verrouille: The tutorial will unlock this building later.

textes.bat.logement.aide: Immigrants settle here in a tent, then the house grows once its needs are met.
textes.bat.deblayer.aide: Removes trees, buildings, roads and ruins, with no refund.
textes.bat.route.aide: Every walker travels on roads: how you lay them out makes or breaks your city.
textes.bat.barriere.aide: Stops walkers on their rounds and lets through those headed somewhere.
textes.bat.puits.aide: Gives well water to houses within 2 tiles. Needs no workers and no road.
textes.bat.fontaine.aide: Gives fountain water within 4 tiles. Must be within 10 tiles of a full reservoir.
textes.bat.reservoir.aide: Fills up at the water's edge, or through an aqueduct from a full reservoir, and feeds fountains.
textes.bat.aqueduc.aide: Carries water from one reservoir to another. It can cross over a road.
textes.bat.ferme_ble.aide: Goes on fertile meadow. Its cart pushers take the wheat to the nearest granary.
textes.bat.grenier.aide: Holds up to 24 loads of food for the markets.
textes.bat.marche.aide: Its buyer goes to the granary or warehouse, and its seller stocks up the houses she passes.
textes.bat.temple_ceres.aide: Its priest gives the houses he passes access to Ceres, goddess of the harvest.
textes.bat.theatre.aide: When an actor arrives, it puts on a 32-day show: its performers bring 15 entertainment points.
textes.bat.colonie_acteurs.aide: Trains actors and sends them to the nearest theater that needs one.
textes.bat.forum.aide: Its tax collector walks past the houses and collects the taxes they have owed since his last visit.
textes.bat.prefecture.aide: Its prefect lowers fire risk and rushes to put out fires within 15 tiles.
textes.bat.ingenieur.aide: Its engineer repairs the buildings he passes and prevents collapses.
textes.bat.ruines.aide: What's left after a fire. Clear them to rebuild.
textes.bat.gravats.aide: What's left after a collapse. Clear it to rebuild.
textes.bat.incendie.aide: Fire can spread to nearby buildings. A prefect puts it out in 2 days.
textes.cause.sansPreneur: storage full, nowhere to send it (granary, warehouse or workshop)
textes.info.terrainVague: Vacant lot: immigrants will settle here if there's room left and they like the city.
textes.info.recensee: Tax collector came by recently: taxes collected
textes.info.nonRecensee: No tax collector for a long time: taxes are piling up (one year at most)
textes.info.bientot: All set: the house is about to grow.
textes.marcheur.immigrant.aide: Comes in by the Road to Rome and settles wherever there's room.
textes.marcheur.emigrant.aide: Unhappy with the city and leaving the map.
textes.marcheur.sansabri.aide: Their house burned down or shrank: they're looking for a new home, or else they'll leave.
textes.marcheur.livreur.aide: Pushes a cart holding one load of goods.
textes.marcheur.acheteuse.aide: Brings one load of food from the granary back to the market.
textes.marcheur.vendeuse.aide: Stocks up the houses she passes, with up to 4 months of food.
textes.marcheur.prefet.aide: Lowers the fire risk of the buildings he passes and puts out fires.
textes.marcheur.percepteur.aide: Collects the taxes each house has built up since his last visit (one year at most).
textes.marcheur.pretre.aide: Gives the houses he passes access to his temple's god.
textes.marcheur.acteur.aide: Goes from the actors' colony to the theater for a new show.
textes.marcheur.comedien.aide: Brings the theater's show to the houses he passes.
textes.terrain.prairieAide: The only land where farms can go.
textes.terrain.eauAide: A reservoir built on the shore fills up by itself.
textes.terrain.romeAide: Immigrants and emigrants pass through here. It can't be removed.
textes.conseil.immigrationArretee: Mood is too low: nobody wants to move in anymore.
textes.calque.eauAide: Light blue: well water. Dark blue: fountain water. The columns show the water at each house.
textes.calque.feuAide: The taller and redder the column, the bigger the fire threat. Only prefects stay visible.
textes.calque.dommagesAide: The taller and redder the column, the more likely the building is to collapse. Only engineers stay visible.
textes.calque.stocksAide: Granaries, markets and warehouses: the taller and greener the column, the fuller they are; red means almost empty. Only cart pushers, haulers, buyers and sellers stay visible.
textes.tuto.ostie.1: Open “Housing” and lay out 10 housing tiles within 2 tiles of the Road to Rome.
textes.tuto.ostie.2: Immigrants come in by the Road to Rome. Wait until you have 24 residents (you can speed up time with +).
textes.tuto.ostie.3: The tents are thirsty: open “Water” and place 2 wells in the middle of your housing.
textes.tuto.ostie.4: With water, a small tent becomes a large tent. Wait until you have 6.
textes.tuto.ostie.5: Your people need bread: place a wheat farm on fertile meadow (the light green), near a road.
textes.tuto.ostie.6: The wheat goes to a granary: build one connected to the farm by road.
textes.tuto.ostie.7: Build a market near the houses: its buyer will go to the granary, and its seller will feed the houses.
textes.tuto.ostie.8: Once fed, tents turn into shacks. Grow 5 houses into small shacks (long-press a house to see what it's missing).
textes.tuto.ostie.9: Final goal: reach 150 residents. Add housing, wells and a 2nd market if needed.
textes.tuto.pompei.1: Tents catch fire easily: open “Security” and build a prefecture along a road.
textes.tuto.pompei.2: Without upkeep, buildings collapse: build an engineer's post.
textes.tuto.pompei.3: To collect taxes, build a forum: its tax collector takes the taxes of the houses he walks past.
textes.tuto.pompei.4: Build a small temple of Ceres near the shacks. Grow 8 houses into large shacks.
textes.tuto.pompei.5: Place a reservoir on the riverbank, connect it by aqueduct to a reservoir in town, then add fountains around it. Grow 8 houses into small hovels.
textes.tuto.pompei.6: Build an actors' colony and a theater: their shows will grow 8 houses into large hovels.
textes.tuto.pompei.7: Final goal: reach 600 residents. Keep an eye on mood and taxes in the Government panel.
textes.tuto.fini: Tutorial complete: the city is yours.

textes.mission.ostie.intro: Rome's port needs workers. On this empty coast, welcome your first settlers: housing, water, bread. The tutorial guides you step by step.
textes.mission.pompei.intro: At the foot of the volcano, the city grows fast and burns just as fast. Protect it from fires and collapses, collect taxes, and give it a temple, fountains and a theater.
textes.briefing.etoiles: 1 star for winning, 1 for getting no help from the emperor, 1 if you win in {mois} months or less.

textes.mission.ravenne.intro: On the edge of the Adriatic lagoons, Ravenna must become a city of craftsmen. Get its workshops going, sell your pottery to the nearby cities and answer the emperor's requests.
textes.mission.narbo.intro: Narbo, the young colony of southern Gaul, opens onto the sea. Forge weapons, build a trade quay and send your ships to Hispania and Ostia.
textes.mission.massalia.intro: Massalia, the great Greek port allied to Rome. Fish, press olive oil, sell it across the Empire and turn the city into a rich and cultured one.

textes.bat.muraille.aide: Stops enemies, who must break it down or go around it. A fortified gate lets a road through.
textes.bat.tour.aide: Built against a wall, it shoots enemies within 6 tiles. It needs guards.
textes.bat.porte.aide: Built across a road: citizens pass, enemies must break it down.
textes.bat.caserne.aide: Trains a recruit every 8 days for the first incomplete fort. A legionary takes one load of weapons.
textes.bat.academie_militaire.aide: Recruits pass through it before reaching their fort and gain one training level.
textes.bat.fort_legionnaires.aide: Houses 16 legionaries, heavy and tough in melee. Tap the fort to give an order. 6 forts at most.
textes.bat.fort_javelots.aide: Houses 16 javelin throwers, who strike from 5 tiles. Tap the fort to give an order. 6 forts at most.
textes.bat.fort_cavaliers.aide: Houses 16 riders, fast to harass the enemy. Tap the fort to give an order. 6 forts at most.

textes.refus.fortsMax: The city already has 6 forts, the maximum.
textes.refus.muraille: A tower must be built against a wall.
textes.refus.moral: The cohort's morale is too low: it is returning to the fort.
textes.refus.soldats: This cohort has no soldiers available.
textes.calque.crimeAide: Red: houses where crime is rising. A passing prefect brings it down.
textes.difficulte.facileAide: More starting funds, fewer enemies, buildings that wear out more slowly, a more patient emperor and gods.
textes.difficulte.normalAide: The game as the mission intends it.
textes.difficulte.difficileAide: Less money, more enemies, buildings that wear out faster, a more demanding emperor and gods.

armee.troupesAbsentes.other: {effectif} soldiers are defending the Empire; back in about {n} months.

msg.villa.other: A house becomes a villa: {n} residents leave to find a home.

msg.invasionAnnonce.other: An army of {effectif} {faction} is marching on the city: it will arrive in {n} months.

textes.msg.invasionFuite: The enemy has lost too much: it is retreating.

msg.invasionFinie.other: The invasion is over; {d} buildings were destroyed.

msg.demandeTroupes.other: The emperor asks for {force} soldiers within {n} months (imperial advisor).

msg.demandeTroupesRappel.other: Reminder: the emperor awaits {force} soldiers, {n} months left.

msg.troupesParties.other: {n} soldiers leave to defend the Empire.

msg.troupesVictoire.other: Victory! The cohort returns with {n} soldiers ({morts} lost); the emperor is pleased.

textes.mission.aquilee.intro: Aquileia guards the Alpine passes. The Gauls are coming down from the mountains: build barracks and a fort before they arrive, forge weapons for Verona and turn the colony into a real city.
textes.mission.vindobona.intro: On the Danube, Vindobona holds the frontier against the Germanic tribes. Their armies grow year after year: raise full cohorts, train them and answer the emperor's calls.
textes.mission.ephese.intro: Ephesus, port of Asia and city of the great temple, dreams of rivalling Athens. Fertile land is scarce here: bring wheat in by sea, build schools, libraries and theatres, and make it a capital of culture.
textes.mission.burdigala.intro: On the banks of the Garonne, Burdigala lives off its vines. Fields are few and northern tribes raid the valley: plant vineyards, sell wine across Gaul and keep the city safe behind its walls.
textes.mission.alexandrie.intro: Alexandria stands between the sea and the desert. The Nile waters only a narrow strip of land: buy wheat from Memphis, keep prefects everywhere, since fire spreads fast under this sun, and make the city the most learned in the Empire.
textes.mission.leptis.intro: Leptis Magna, the city of olive oil, stretches between the sea and the desert. Numidian horsemen strike from the south, fast and many: import your wheat, press oil for Rome and put your forts in their path.
textes.mission.corinthe.intro: Rome refounds Corinth on its ruins, between two seas. The earth often shakes here, and whole districts can collapse at once: keep money aside to rebuild and make the city a great market of Greece.
textes.mission.colonia.intro: Colonia Agrippina guards the Rhine. On the far bank, the Germanic tribes gather ever larger armies, and the bridge is their way in: hold it, raise legions and feed a city that grows under threat.
textes.mission.antioche.intro: Antioch, the great city of the East, draws the richest families of the Empire. Build patrician districts, villas then palaces, surrounded by gardens, temples and shows, and give it a hippodrome worthy of it.
textes.mission.palmyre.intro: Palmyra, the caravan oasis, lives on trade between Rome and the East. Parthian horse archers attack from the east: protect your wells and roads, buy your wheat and drive back ever larger armies.
textes.mission.athenes.intro: Athens, mother of the arts and philosophy, awaits its governor. Here everything counts: culture, wealth, peace and the emperor's favour, at the highest thresholds of the campaign. It is your final trial before the title of Princeps.
textes.mission.eburacum.intro: At the edge of the Empire, Eburacum holds Britain against the Picts. Their war bands come down from the north through the forests: build a strong, prosperous city and become Princeps at the end of the world.
textes.aide.eauRequise: It needs a full reservoir close by.
textes.campagne.texte: You have won all 10 tiers: Rome names you Princeps. {n} stars out of {max}.
textes.campagne.suite: Replay the other province of a tier to earn its stars, or build freely on a map you have already won.
textes.aide.debut.texte: Lay roads from the road to Rome, then housing tiles along them: families arrive by the road and settle. Give them water, food and services so their houses grow. The advisor always says what is missing, and tapping a building explains what is holding it back.
textes.aide.routes.texte: Almost every building needs a road within 2 tiles. Its workers set out along the roads: roamers (prefects, priests, market sellers…) head for the houses and buildings that need them, the most urgent and the nearest first, and serve everything they pass; a street with no needs is skipped. The others head straight for their goal. A roadblock stops roamers but lets everyone else through: it keeps services inside a district.
textes.aide.maisons.texte: A house goes up a level when all its needs are met, and goes down if one of them is missing for too long. From tent to insula, each level asks a little more: water, varied food, religion, shows, goods, services and a nicer neighbourhood (desirability). Large houses spread over 2 × 2 tiles by taking in their neighbours. Tap a house: it tells you what it needs to grow.
textes.aide.eau.texte: A well gives water to nearby houses. A fountain, which is better, must be connected to a full reservoir. A reservoir fills up beside a river or the sea, or through an aqueduct coming from another reservoir that has water. Baths need a reservoir too. The “Water” overlay shows what is covered.
textes.aide.nourriture.texte: Farms are placed on fertile meadows: the richer the soil, the more they produce. Their carts deliver to the nearest granary; the market buyer fetches food there and the market sellers carry it to the houses. Rich houses want several foods. Without meadows, buy wheat from neighbouring cities: it arrives in the warehouses, then goes to the granaries.
textes.aide.travail.texte: Residents of working age fill the jobs; a building short of workers slows down or stops. When hands are short, the priorities (labour advisor) decide who is served first. Unemployment, high taxes or wages below Rome’s lower the mood, and unhappy residents leave. Patricians do not work.
textes.aide.industrie.texte: A quarry, a mine, a timber camp, an olive grove or a vineyard produces a raw material; the workshop next door turns it into goods (pottery, furniture, oil, wine, weapons). Warehouses keep materials and goods; their orders (accept, refuse, fetch, empty) and limits decide what goes in. The market sells goods to the houses that ask for them.
textes.aide.securite.texte: Every building builds up a risk of fire and collapse: a prefect or an engineer walking past resets it. A building that burns or collapses leaves ruins, and fire sometimes spreads to its neighbours, faster in a dry climate. Poor, unhappy districts attract thieves; prefects arrest them, but high crime turns into riots. The earth can also shake and flatten a district.
textes.aide.finances.texte: Every month, each inhabited house owes that month's tax, at the rate set in Government; the forum tax collector takes everything it owes when he walks past (one year of arrears at most). Wages, building, imports, festivals and the tribute to Rome come out of the treasury, and sales to other cities go in. Below zero, the emperor bails the treasury out once (relief), which costs the second star; debt costs interest, and beyond 5,000 denarii of debt nothing more can be built.
textes.aide.religion.texte: Ceres (harvests), Neptune (sea), Mercury (trade), Mars (army) and Venus (happiness) each want temples, in proportion to the population, and festivals. A delighted god grants a blessing; a jealous or neglected god grows angry: lost harvest, sunken ships, an emptied warehouse, disheartened legions, gloomy citizens. The gods advisor shows each one’s mood.
textes.aide.culture.texte: Theatres, amphitheatres, colosseums and the hippodrome put on shows when their performers come from their school (actors’ colony, gladiator school, lion house, chariot maker). Schools, libraries and academies educate residents; barbers, baths, doctors and hospitals keep them healthy, or an epidemic may break out. The culture rating counts the places in temples, theatres, libraries, schools and academies per resident.
textes.aide.commerce.texte: The map of the Empire (Trade button in the top bar) shows the cities and, next to each one, what it buys and what it sells; opening a route is paid once. For each good, choose: import, export, reserve or nothing, and how much to keep. Caravans call at the warehouses near the town entrance; ships dock at the trade quay. Each city trades a limited amount per year.
textes.aide.empereur.texte: The emperor’s favour drops a little every year. It rises when you meet his requests on time (goods, denarii, troops) and when you give him a gift from your personal fortune. Your governor’s salary adds to that fortune, which you keep from one mission to the next. Favour that stays too low for too long sends his legions against your city.
textes.aide.cotes.texte: A mission is won when the population and the four ratings (culture, prosperity, peace, favour) reach their thresholds together. Prosperity is recalculated in January: profit, jobs, wages, rich houses, varied food; it never goes above the average value of the houses. Peace rises each year without riots or destruction. The ratings advisor says what holds each one back.
textes.aide.armee.texte: An invasion is announced on the map of the Empire a few months before it arrives. The barracks train recruits with weapons; each fort raises a cohort of 16 soldiers (legionaries, javelin throwers or cavalry), which the military academy trains further. Tap a fort to give an order: march, change formation, return. Walls, towers and gates stop or slow the enemy.
textes.aide.patriciens.texte: Beyond the insula, wealthy families build villas and then palaces, from 2 × 2 to 4 × 4 tiles: they ask for wine, a hospital, several gods, great shows and a very fine neighbourhood. They pay a lot of tax but do not work: you need enough plebeians to keep the city running. The senate, the governor’s residence and the hippodrome round off a great city.
textes.voisins.intro: Found a province together: each player builds their own city on their own device, at their own pace, and you trade as neighbours. The province wins when every active city reaches its goals.
textes.voisins.attente: Connecting to the province trading post…
textes.voisins.pleine: This province is full: all 4 cities are taken.
textes.voisins.serveur: The trading post is not answering. Provinces are played on freemicrogames.com, with a connection.
textes.voisins.codeInvalide: This code doesn't look right: 6 letters or digits.
textes.voisins.codeAide: Give this code to your friends: each one takes a free city of the province, whenever they like. They can also use the Friends page of the site.
textes.voisins.enLigne: Online: trade with your neighbours is open.
textes.voisins.horsLigne: Offline: routes to your neighbours are closed.
textes.voisins.gagneeTexte: Every active city has reached its goals. Well done, governors!

voisins.reserve.one: {n} cartload is waiting at the gate for warehouse space.
voisins.reserve.other: {n} cartloads are waiting at the gate for warehouse space.

textes.voisins.absent: Away for more than 7 days: a computer city trades in their place; their stall stays open.
textes.voisins.envoyerSignal: Send a signal to your neighbours
textes.voisins.part: {nom}: {pop} residents, {ventes} denarii of sales to neighbours
textes.voisins.ficheJoueur: A city of a player in your province: you trade through the trading post, at the price between players.

textes.signal.route: Open a route to my city.
textes.province.campanie.desc: The wheat fields and vineyards of Capua, the fishing port of Puteoli, the marble and olive groves of Nola, the forests of Salernum.
textes.province.hispanie.desc: The fish-rich coast of Saguntum, the wheat plains of Valentia, the forests of Dertosa, the iron and marble of Ilerda.

msg.prov.livraison.other: A caravan from {voisin} brings {n} cartloads ({deniers} denarii).

textes.msg.prov.enLigne: Province trading post reached: routes to your neighbours are open.
textes.msg.prov.horsLigne: Trading post unreachable: routes to your neighbours are closed.

textes.mission.dertosa.atouts: Rich in timber, clay · short of olives, marble, fish

textes.commerce.toucheCite: Tap a city on the map: its sheet opens here, with the price of the road.
textes.missions.carteAide: Tap a city on the map to read its mission. The number is its tier; gold cities are won.

tutoB.nouveauxIntro.one: In this mission you can build {n} building you don't know yet. Tap it to learn what it does and what to do.
tutoB.nouveauxIntro.other: In this mission you can build {n} buildings you don't know yet. Tap one to learn what it does and what to do.

textes.tutoB.menuAide: In the menu, the "New" mark stays on the ones you haven't read yet.
textes.tutoB.route: Place it within 2 tiles of a road: its workers and carters go that way.
textes.tutoB.employes: It needs {n} workers: they come from inhabited houses, so you need enough people (labour advisor).
textes.tutoB.prairie: Place it on meadow (dark green grass): the more fertile the land, the bigger the harvest.
textes.tutoB.pres.arbres: Place it right next to trees: its woodcutters fell them.
textes.tutoB.pres.eau: Place it on the shore (river or sea): that's where the clay is.
textes.tutoB.pres.rochers: Place it against rocks (grey stones): the rock is dug there.
textes.tutoB.fermeAliment: Its harvest ({bien}) goes to the nearest granary: build a granary linked by road, then a market near the houses.
textes.tutoB.fermeMatiere: Its harvest ({bien}) goes to the warehouse; a "{atelier}" turns it into {produit}, which markets sell or you export.
textes.tutoB.extraction: It produces {bien} ({n} loads a year), stored in the warehouse: build a warehouse linked by road.
textes.tutoB.vendre: You can also sell it to other cities (Trade button at the top).
textes.tutoB.atelier: It turns {matiere} into {produit}. The raw material comes from "{source}" or is bought from other cities.
textes.tutoB.atelierImport: It turns {matiere} into {produit}. Here the raw material is bought from other cities (Trade button at the top).
textes.tutoB.entrepotAtelier: You need a warehouse linked by road: its carters bring the raw material to the workshop and take away what it makes.
textes.tutoB.peche: Place it on the shore, near a shoal of fish (ripples in the water): its boat goes fishing.
textes.tutoB.pecheGrenier: The fish goes to the granary, like wheat: you need a granary and a market.
textes.tutoB.entrepot1: It stores raw materials and goods (8 slots): workshops, markets and caravans come to use it.
textes.tutoB.entrepot2: Put it near the town entrance for trade; tap it to set what it accepts, refuses or fetches.
textes.tutoB.grenier: Farms and fishermen deliver food here; market buyers come to collect it. Put it between the farms and the districts.
textes.tutoB.marche1: Put it among the houses: its seller goes from house to house, first where things are most lacking.
textes.tutoB.marche2: Its buyer fetches food from the granary and goods from the warehouse (40 road tiles at most).
textes.tutoB.service: Its worker ({marcheur}) walks the streets to the houses that need him and serves everything within 2 tiles: put it in the heart of the district.
textes.tutoB.prefet: The prefect lowers the fire risk and runs to put out fires. Build one in each district: the "Fire" overlay shows buildings in danger.
textes.tutoB.ingenieur: He repairs buildings; without him they wear out and collapse. The "Damage" overlay shows where he is missing.
textes.tutoB.impot: Its tax collector takes the tax each house has owed since his last visit: without him, no taxes (rate in Government).
textes.tutoB.religion: Houses need temples to grow, and {dieu} wants enough temples to stay happy (gods advisor).
textes.tutoB.education: Houses need it to go up a level: tap a house to see what it is missing.
textes.tutoB.sante: Houses need it to go up a level, and the city is better protected from epidemics.
textes.tutoB.marbre: You also need {n} loads of marble in a warehouse to build it (marble quarry or purchase).
textes.tutoB.eau: It needs a full reservoir close by.
textes.tutoB.spectacle: It needs performers: also build "{ecoles}". They come to perform here, then its worker ({marcheur}) brings the show to the houses.
textes.tutoB.ecoleArt: It trains performers ({artiste}), who go to perform in "{lieux}": build them on the same road network.
textes.tutoB.puits: It gives water to houses within 2 tiles. No road or workers needed: put one in the middle of each group of tents.
textes.tutoB.fontaine: Place it within 10 tiles of a full reservoir: it gives better water to houses within 4 tiles, which they need to grow.
textes.tutoB.reservoir1: Put it on the edge of a river, lake or the sea so it fills up; or link it with an aqueduct to an already full reservoir.
textes.tutoB.reservoir2: A full reservoir feeds fountains and baths within 10 tiles ("Water" overlay).
textes.tutoB.aqueduc: Draw it from a full reservoir to another reservoir: the water flows through it. It can cross over a road.
textes.tutoB.deco: It makes the district nicer: nearby houses gain desirability, which they need to move up.
textes.tutoB.place: Draw it on an existing road: the road stays usable and the neighbouring houses become nicer.
textes.tutoB.barriere: Put it on a road: it stops workers on their rounds (prefects, sellers…) and keeps them in their district; carters and residents pass.
textes.tutoB.residence: It makes the surroundings very desirable: put it in the heart of the fine districts. Only one per city.
textes.tutoB.oracle: It honours all five gods at once, with no road or workers: put it where it makes houses nicer.
textes.tutoB.quai1: Place it on the shore, one side on the water: ships on sea routes dock there.
textes.tutoB.quai2: Then open a sea route (Trade button at the top); its dockers carry loads between the ship and the warehouses.
textes.tutoB.caserne: It trains the recruits for your forts; a legionary takes a load of weapons: keep weapons in a warehouse (weapons workshop or purchase).
textes.tutoB.academieMil: Recruits pass through it before joining their fort and fight better: put it between the barracks and the forts.
textes.tutoB.fort: It houses a cohort of 16 soldiers ({unite}), trained by the barracks. Tap the fort to give an order: go, formation, return.
textes.tutoB.tour: Put it against a wall: its guards shoot enemies within 6 tiles.
textes.tutoB.muraille: Draw it around the city, on the side enemies come from (map of the Empire): they must break it or go around.
textes.tutoB.porte: Put it across a road that goes through the wall: residents pass, enemies must break it down.
textes.tutoB.calque: To see where its worker goes, open the overlays (button at the top): the building stays visible, and so does the worker.
